name: Ingrid Lindgren
headline: 34-year-old owner of a boutique hotel, caring for her mother in Stockholm, Sweden
title: Sillunch Invitation
situation: Ingrid's longtime friend Maja calls to invite her to the monthly sillunch – a traditional Swedish herring lunch at a cellar restaurant in Gamla Stan. The group will eat pickled herring, drink snaps, and sing snapsvisor together. Maja mentions that everyone really hopes Ingrid can make it this Saturday at noon. Ingrid's mother's night nurse is off that day, but her mother can manage a few hours on her own or with a quick neighbor check-in. Ingrid must decide whether to accept the invitation and join the cultural ritual or decline with a polite excuse.

context.relationship_profiles: Maja has known Ingrid since primary school in Uppsala and still sends her handwritten birthday cards despite Ingrid rarely replying. The two used to sing snapsvisor together at student gatherings before Ingrid inherited the hotel. Maja has never complained about Ingrid's cancellations but always asks if the hotel can spare her.
context.tendencies: When attending regional conferences, Ingrid skips the after-dinner socializing to call the night nurse and check on her mother. She has declined three prior monthly sillunch invitations in a row with brief but polite excuses about hotel obligations. In business negotiations she calculates trade-offs carefully; with personal invitations she often decides based on her mother's mood that morning.
context.current_state: Ingrid has just finished tallying the occupancy for the week and is satisfied that revenue is slightly above projection. She feels a low-level fatigue from managing a guest who complained about the heating in suite 4. Her mother had a calm morning and is dozing in the courtyard-facing room.
context.immediate_memories: The phrase 'cellar restaurant in Gamla Stan' brings back the memory of her first visit there with her mother, eating herring while her mother talked about working in a library. Maja's mention of 'snapsvisor' reminds her of the evening before her grandparents' funeral, when she drank snaps with family friends and let herself laugh.
context.reflective_memories: She remembers that every time she has skipped a cultural ritual like this, she later felt a quiet regret about losing touch with her roots. Her mother used to say that sillunch was a way to slow down winter, and Ingrid has never forgotten that remark.
